knowledge_point.title: Sketching a Line Using Two Points

question.:question/problem: Which of the following graphs shows the line $y=-4x?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We need to find two distinct points that lie on our line. Any two points will do!

- For the first point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=0.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4x \\  & =-4(0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the first point is $(0,0).$

- For the second point, we will let the $x$-coordinate be $x=1.$ Then the $y$-coordinate is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4x \\  & =-4(1) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second point is $(1,-4).$

Finally, we plot those two points on the $xy$-plane and draw a line through them. This is the graph of $y=-4x.$ 

![](images/8b/8b008b94eebbd24ae51670447848ce2d644c067d43dd92d72de85b048358cc54.png)

generation.domain: x real; two distinct points; bounded negative slopes
